decisions.question: How should the coordinator handle long-running tasks that exceed a single Claude session (~200k token context window, 30-120 min pipeline runs)?

options.label: Checkpoint/resume: save coordinator state to orchestrator, resume on new session
Stateless coordinator: read full pipeline state from orchestrator on each invocation
Hybrid: periodic state snapshots with stateless fallback

decisions.question: How should gateway phase enforcement work when the coordinator can dynamically skip/reorder phases?

options.label: New coordinator phase: a dedicated phase with broad permissions covering all coordinator operations
Dynamic phase switching: coordinator requests phase transitions via orchestrator API, gateway follows
Relaxed enforcement: coordinator role exempted from phase restrictions (but not merge/branch restrictions)

decisions.question: What should the coordinator be able to do without human approval?

options.label: Minimal: spawn agents and monitor only; all workflow decisions need approval
Moderate: spawn agents, skip phases, loop back; PR creation needs approval
Full autonomy: everything except merge; human approves the final PR only

decisions.question: How much of the coordinator system should be built in the first iteration?

options.label: Coordinator agent + orchestrator API extensions only (no MCP, no Claude Code integration)
Coordinator agent + MCP server (enables Claude Code session integration)
Full system: coordinator + MCP + Claude Code integration + async triggers

questions.question: What cost limits or guardrails should be applied to coordinator sessions? (e.g., max agents per task, max total token budget, max wall-clock time)
What should happen when the coordinator session crashes mid-task with running agents?
Should the coordinator be able to manage multiple related issues simultaneously, or is one-issue-at-a-time sufficient for v1?
How should users interact with the coordinator — via Slack, GitHub issue comments, a dedicated CLI, or the existing egg command? What is the expected UX for submitting tasks and receiving updates?
